lines: 1,080 people starred a pixel-art space station. Its crew? Real AI agents.
StarNet is a local-first desktop app, and the station isn't decoration.
The layout you draw is the workflow the agents run. Rooms are teams. Hallways are handoff lanes. Placed objects are real capability grants.
Several agents run at once. Real model calls, real tools, real cost.
Night Shift keeps them working while you're away, on an adjustable leash. Every away-action is logged.
Unclear task? It asks one question with options, over Telegram or Slack, instead of guessing.
No simulated work, no simulated spend. The interface never shows what the harness can't prove.
It's 92% JavaScript. The sidecar uses Node core modules only, so nothing to install.
Clone the repo, run one Node command, open localhost 8787, and bring your own key.
No key, no bill: pull qwen3 8B in Ollama. Expect about 10 GB of graphics memory.
Coming from OpenClaw or Hermes? StarNet imports your agent.
StarNet. Your machine, your data, your crew.
